close_reason: Applied path (a) from bead body: replaced 'streamed by the HTTP client without an explicit cap' with the accurate description (buffered via reqwest RequestBuilder::json -> serde_json::to_vec) and noted the transient ~3-4x peak. The 'callers may prefer to batch' guidance is retained but its rationale now correctly points at the transient memory peak. Edit landed in 8c85232. Pre-commit gate passed: cargo fmt, cargo clippy -p jmap-metadata-client --tests -- -D warnings, cargo test -p jmap-metadata-client (9/9), RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings cargo doc -p jmap-metadata-client --no-deps. Out-of-scope paths (b) richer transport-internals docs, (c) base-client request_body cap intentionally not pursued — both are expansion paths, not the minimum-correct fix the bead labelled 'Cheapest fix'.
description:
src/methods/metadata.rs:185-196 — the # Errors rustdoc section added in commit d0a0bd4 contains a factually wrong claim about wire-transport behaviour:

    The size of `update` is otherwise bounded only by available memory;
    the wire request is streamed by the HTTP client without an explicit
    cap. Callers dealing with thousands of patches per call may prefer
    to batch across multiple `metadata_set` invocations to bound
    per-request memory pressure.

The "streamed by the HTTP client" half is wrong. The transport path is:

  1. metadata_set serializes the update HashMap into a serde_json::Value
     via serde_json::to_value (line 216) — allocates a full JSON tree in
     memory.
  2. build_request packages it into a JmapRequest (line 228).
  3. self.call_internal -> JmapClient::call (crate-jmap-base-client/src/client.rs:342)
     calls reqwest::RequestBuilder::json(req) (line 353).
  4. reqwest's .json() implementation is, in every version on
     crates.io (0.11.27 / 0.12.28 / 0.13.2 verified locally under
     ~/.cargo/registry/), literally:

       match serde_json::to_vec(json) { Ok(body) => { ... } }

     i.e. it buffers the ENTIRE serialized request body into a Vec<u8>
     upfront before sending. The reqwest API does support streaming
     bodies via Body::wrap_stream / Body::from(Stream), but
     RequestBuilder::json does NOT use it.

So the actual peak-memory cost of a metadata_set call with a large
update map is roughly:

  - HashMap<Id, PatchObject> in caller memory
  - serde_json::Value tree (≈ same order of magnitude as the HashMap)
  - serde_json::to_vec output Vec<u8> inside reqwest
  - reqwest's internal request representation

…which is approximately 3-4× the in-memory size of the HashMap at the
peak of metadata_set, not "memory-bounded by the HashMap alone, with
the wire body streamed out".

Why this matters for the contract:

  1. Callers reading "streamed by the HTTP client without an explicit
     cap" will reasonably size their update HashMap assuming the
     transport will drain it as it serializes, which is the standard
     HTTP-streaming memory profile. They will allocate update maps
     that approach the OS memory limit, and metadata_set will OOM at
     the to_vec or json() step rather than midway through a streamed
     send.

  2. The recommended workaround in the same doc-comment ("batch across
     multiple metadata_set invocations") is the right advice but for
     the wrong reason. Callers should batch because each call has a
     transient 3-4× memory peak, not because of a non-existent
     in-flight streaming cap.

  3. wzq9.26 was closed with the close-reason 'Documents that the
     wire request is streamed without a cap' — that close-reason
     accepted the factually wrong claim. This finding records that
     the underlying doc is still inaccurate after wzq9.26 closed.

Fix paths (in order of caller value):

  (a) Replace "streamed by the HTTP client" with "buffered by the HTTP
      client" and note the transient 3-4× peak. Cheapest fix.
  (b) Additionally document that reqwest's RequestBuilder::json
      serializes the full body upfront and that the peak memory cost is
      the HashMap + serde_json::Value + serialized Vec<u8> at the same
      time.
  (c) (Out of scope for this crate; tracked separately if pursued.)
      Add a request_body cap to jmap-base-client ClientConfig analogous
      to max_call_body (response cap). That is a base-client design
      change, not a metadata-client doc fix.

Workspace-wide propagation: the same "streamed" claim is likely on
canonical jmap-mail-client::email_set if the # Errors section was
copied. Check before fixing here only.

Cross-ref:
  - wzq9.26 (closed, but underlying claim still wrong)
  - wzq9.31 (broader # Errors-section coverage gap on the other 4
    methods)
  - jmap-base-client/src/client.rs:342-375 (JmapClient::call — actual
    transport)
  - reqwest source: ~/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-*/reqwest-0.13.2/src/async_impl/request.rs::pub fn json
title: metadata_set # Errors doc-comment claims wire request is 'streamed by the HTTP client' — actually buffered (reqwest .json() calls serde_json::to_vec)
